6do6v9:198: : The core innovation of Vercel Connect is not better key management (vault), but completely eliminating the need to store tokens. In traditional architectures, agents hold long-lived provider tokens—even if stored in a vault, once leaked, attackers gain full-permission access. Connect shifts authentication from "holding secrets" to "proving identity": agents hold no secrets at all, and every time they need access, they prove their identity via OIDC to obtain short-term, task-scoped credentials.
6g1mna:118: : If you're building agents in the Vercel ecosystem, Connect + eve is the best combination—eve handles agent orchestration, Connect handles external service authentication, and AI Gateway handles LLM routing. This layered architecture is more maintainable than a single-platform approach.
90m1iq:170: : Connect is not a standalone product—it is the security layer of the Vercel agent ecosystem (eve framework + AI Gateway + Connect). eve agents obtain external service credentials through Connect and route LLM calls through AI Gateway, forming a complete "agent security runtime". This layered design is more flexible than a single "agent platform".
